messages:
maria: Quick Q: for the embeddings batch endpoint, what's our official contract if some items fail validation or get deduped? Do we preserve input order and return null entries, drop them, or return a mapping? Need a decision so SDKs + ingestion pipelines behave consistently.
aj: I vote preserve order — always return a vectors array with the same length as the input. Use null for failed items and include an errors map keyed by input index. Example we can put in the spec:```json
{
  "vectors": [ [0.012, -0.34, ...], null, [0.21, 0.03, ...] ],
  "errors": { "1": "TOO_LONG" },
  "applied_transforms": [ "truncated:10000" ]
}
```
devon: +1 to preserve order. One edge we need to decide: the serving runtime may dedupe or reorder for perf. If we do reorder internally, we must expose an index_map in the response that maps returned positions -> original input positions, or set a header indicating reordering. Otherwise clients will misalign embeddings.
maria: prefer to avoid reordering complexity unless necessary. Proposal: default contract = preserve order and same-length vectors. If we absolutely need to dedupe/reorder, require the server to set header `X-Embed-Reordered: 1` and include a top-level `index_map` array. Also, for per-item validation vs batch-level rejection: do we want atomic batches (reject whole batch if > limit) or partial successes?
aj: partial per-item validation is more useful for ingestion flows. Returning 200 with vectors + errors feels simpler than 207. For exceeding max batch size, return 413 with JSON body explaining `max_items`. Eg:```json
{
  "error": "BATCH_TOO_LARGE",
  "max_items": 1000
}
```
devon: can we also add a response header like `X-Embed-Policy: truncation=truncate_to_10000;dedupe=disabled` so clients can know what transforms were applied? Would help for telemetry.
maria: agreed. Let's formalize a minimal contract to put in the API spec: 1) By default, embeddings endpoint preserves input order and returns a `vectors` array of the same length as the request, with `null` placeholders for items that failed validation; 2) When the server reorders/dedupes for optimization, it MUST set `X-Embed-Reordered: 1` and return `index_map` mapping response indices -> original indices; 3) If request exceeds `max_items`, respond 413 with `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` and `max_items` in the body (no partial success); 4) Include `applied_transforms` in successful responses and `X-Embed-Policy` header for transforms applied. I'll open a docs PR with this wording. @aj can you update SDK behavior to map null -> None and to accept index_map when present? :thumbsup:
aj: On it. I'll add SDK changes and tests to handle nulls + `index_map`. Will include a migration note. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
